evidence: dtos.ts defines OrderDto, StockLevelDto, PlaceOrderRequest and the only mappers, toOrderDto and toStockLevelDto. All six use-case files import from it.
AdvanceOrderUseCase, CancelOrderUseCase, GetOrderUseCase, ListOrdersByStateUseCase, ListStockLevelsUseCase and PlaceOrderUseCase all use the same shape: constructor-injected ports plus execute().
list-orders-by-state-use-case.ts leaves state checking to the domain's assertOrderState instead of repeating it.
advance-, cancel- and get-order-use-case.ts each repeat `findById` + `throw new NotFoundError(`Order ${orderId} not found`)`. This is minor lookup boilerplate, not a business invariant.
place-order-use-case.ts checks the unknown request input (customerId, items, productId) inline before building OrderItem and Order, which is the application layer's normal job at its boundary.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module's files serve one concern: application use cases for orders and stock levels. Each one is a class with constructor-injected domain ports (OrderRepository, ProductRepository, StockReservationService, IdGenerator) and a single execute method. Every use case returns DTOs built by the shared mappers in dtos.ts (toOrderDto, toStockLevelDto), so no file builds DTOs by hand or bypasses the module's abstractions. ListOrdersByStateUseCase leaves state checking to the domain (assertOrderState), so that rule is not repeated. Two minor points do not reach a violation. First, three use cases repeat the same findById-then-throw-NotFoundError check; this is lookup boilerplate rather than a business invariant copied out of its proper home. Second, PlaceOrderUseCase checks its input inline, which fits the application layer's job of validating unknown request data before building domain objects. There is no split into unrelated concerns and no clear duplicated invariant.
